cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players experience slow initial progression and must keep the game open for passive gains.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a very slow progression speed and requires waiting extended periods of time to advance.

citations.review_text: If you are thinking of buying this for a quick dopamine hit, I would suggest looking for a different game, the progression is not as fast as other incremental games, even if youre using an auto clicker. I am determined to reach high numbers tho. Recommended for achievements hunters too

A cozy and quaint incremental idle game that seems stuck in the past. Reading other reviews, maybe there is some nostalgia factor missing for me, since I didn't play this when it first released in 2013 (13 years ago at the time of review). I feel like today, there are more enjoyable options in this genre.

+++ Vibes are really good. Music is great, UI is fancy with lots of flourishes.

-- The font size is extremely small, and there is no way to increase it. I was unable to actually read most of the text in this game due to visual disability, and it significantly affected my ability to play. For example, upgrade description text was unreadable.

--- Cookies do not progress offline, you have to keep the game open in the background. Very strange decision for an idle game of this genre.

--- The game is a slow burn. An extremely slow burn. You'll be waiting actual hours to make tiny progress, and the first additional mechanic you unlock takes 24 hours before you can even use it. After 6 hours, I've only unlocked a few buildings and seemingly hit a soft cap. Personally, this frustrated me. Others may enjoy it.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that active clicking is mostly limited to the opening phase, after which the game shifts to buying buildings and upgrades.

citations.review_text:
You click the cookie to get more cookies. You buy buildings which make cookies for you, so you don't have to click the cookie so much. You upgrade the buildings so they make more cookies per second. Simple, right? Except, some time later, you've ascended several times, seen eldritch horrors beyond comprehension, made a pact with Satan, God and all of their demons and angels, turned the entire universe (and all other, parallel universes) into raw cookie dough, and learned several new numbers along the way (what the heck is a quattuordecillion?!).

10/10, would click the cookie again. T̴̲̈́h̸̲̀e̴̯̕ ̴̘̈c̶͛ͅo̸͕̐ŏ̸͔k̷͙̒i̴̘̓e̴̟͠ ̵̣́i̵̧͛s̵͈̿ ̸̞̂e̵̮̓t̵̩̾ĕ̴̪ȑ̸̗n̵̬͝ḁ̸̓l̸̜̅.̸͚̈́

This game is complete nonsense and utterly brilliant. Number go up is the hook. But it is done with humour and engaging silliness. I currently have over 100 grandmas helping me bake cookies, along with any amount of banks, temples, etc. funding the process. The game is also somewhat misnamed in the sense that you don't do very much clicking after the first few minutes, after a while you just need to check in now and again to buy upgrades to make even more insane amounts of cookies. In the end you will consume the universe with your baking enterprise.
